title: Genetics Flashcards
description: Key facts from TNPSC Group II Zoology Genetics Chapter

cards.q: Who is known as the Father of Genetics?
cards.a: G.J. Mendel.

cards.q: In which year was Mendel born and where?
cards.a: 1822 in Czechoslovakia (Heinzendorf, Silesia).

cards.q: For how many years did Mendel conduct his research and where?
cards.a: 9 years (1856-1865) in Brunn.

cards.q: Which plant did Mendel use for his experiments?
cards.a: Pisum sativum (Garden Peas).

cards.q: How many characters did Mendel study out of the total available?
cards.a: 7 characters out of 34.

cards.q: What is the phenotypic ratio of a monohybrid cross?
What is the genotypic ratio of a monohybrid cross?
What is the phenotypic ratio of a dihybrid cross?
Who made the square to prove Mendel's results and what is it called?
cards.a: Punnett made it; it is called the Punnett Square or Chequered Square.

cards.q: Who rediscovered Mendel's work in 1900?
cards.a: Hugo de Vries (Holland), Carl Correns (Germany), and Erich Von Tschermak (Austria).

cards.q: Who discovered Jumping Genes and on which organism?
cards.a: Barbara McClintock, working on Maize.

cards.q: What are Jumping Genes also called?
cards.a: Transposable elements, transposons, or insertion elements.

cards.q: What is the difference between homozygous and heterozygous?
cards.a: Homozygous has identical alleles (TT, tt); Heterozygous has dissimilar alleles (Tt).

cards.q: What is Gene Therapy?
cards.a: Replacement of corrective genes in place of defective genes in humans.

cards.q: What are the two types of Gene Therapy?
cards.a: Somatic cell gene therapy and Germ line cell gene therapy.

cards.q: How many pairs of chromosomes do humans have?
cards.a: 23 pairs (Male: XY, Female: XX).

cards.q: What are Restriction Enzymes also called?
cards.a: Genetic Scissors or Restriction Endonucleases.

cards.q: What is DNA Ligase called in genetic engineering?
cards.a: Molecular Paste.

cards.q: What is the most famous cloned mammal?
cards.a: Dolly the Sheep.

cards.q: What is the difference between Totipotent and Pluripotent stem cells?
cards.a: Totipotent can give rise to all 220 cell types plus extra-embryonic cells (placenta); Pluripotent can give rise to all body cell types but NOT the placenta.

cards.q: What is the 21st century called in relation to genetics?
cards.a: The Gene Century.

cards.q: What is a Test Cross?
cards.a: A cross between an organism whose genotype is unknown and an organism that is homozygous recessive for that trait.

cards.q: Name the Mendelian genetic disorders.
cards.a: Haemophilia, Sickle Cell Anaemia, and Phenylketonuria.

cards.q: Name the Chromosomal genetic disorders.
cards.a: Down's Syndrome, Klinefelter's Syndrome, and Turner's Syndrome.

cards.q: What is a Bio-Sensor?
cards.a: A device which uses a living organism or biological molecules (enzymes or antibodies) to detect the presence of chemicals.
